meta.title: Halloween DJ Party — 5-Hour Theme-Park DJ Programming & Execution Manual
source: PDF manual provided by the PO, 2026-09-28 (Halloween_DJ_Party.pdf)
meta.programmingConcept: House → Tribal / Latin House → Dark Tech House → Electro House, with Halloween markers used strategically rather than continuously.
meta.audience: Mixed Latin + American crowd. Primary objective: preserve danceable continuity while maintaining a clear Halloween identity.
meta.masterArchitecture: Warm Up ≈ 2h · Headliner ≈ 2.5h · Closer ≈ 30m · plus Reserve / Quick Exit.
meta.operatingPrinciple: This is a programming map, not a command to play every track from beginning to end. Use phrasing, extended intros/outros, loops and clean edits to control timing. Halloween records are impact points. Between them, maintain groove with House, Tribal/Latin and Tech House so the event feels like a professional DJ performance rather than a novelty playlist. Keep one main Thriller payoff. Do not stack multiple Halloween anthems back-to-back. Protect the energy curve and always keep the Reserve crate available.
meta.notes: BPM y Energy no vienen en el manual del PO por track individual, solo un rango objetivo por bloque. Varios tracks se repiten entre bloques a propósito (son puntos de conexión/groove reutilizados entre marcadores de Halloween, tal como los describe el propio manual) — transcritos tal cual, sin deduplicar. BPM real investigado el 2026-09-28 en fuentes públicas (Tunebat, SongBPM, GetSongBPM, Beatport, Mixgraph, Runhundred) para los tracks identificables — cada uno con su `bpmSource`. Se dejó en null a propósito, sin adivinar, en tres casos: (1) el track no aparece indexado en ninguna fuente pública real; (2) fuentes en conflicto entre sí sin un valor confiable (ej. Monster Mash, Sympathy for the Devil, Pjanoo); (3) remixes/edits que cambian de género (Tech House Remix, House Edit) donde solo se encontró el BPM del original, no el de esa versión específica — aplicar el BPM del original ahí sería un dato inventado. Confirmar en vivo con Serato antes del evento real, mismo criterio que Reparto/90's Hit's. Reserve/Quick Exit no tiene columna de BPM en la UI todavía — no se le agregó BPM en esta pasada. Cambios de tracklist a pedido del PO (2026-09-28): 'I Put a Spell on You' (Screamin' Jay Hawkins) reemplazado por 'Black Magic Woman / Gypsy Queen' (Santana) — mismo criterio de PO, no le gustan los gritos del original. 'Clint Eastwood' (Gorillaz) y 'Zombie' (The Cranberries) reemplazados por 'Ghost Town' (The Specials) y 'Werewolves of London' (Warren Zevon) — ambos originales tenían BPM real en conflicto grave entre fuentes (posible detección a mitad/doble tiempo), los reemplazos tienen BPM real limpio y consistente en todas las fuentes.

sections.name: Warm Up
sections.howToUse: Begin cinematic and spacious while guests enter and explore. During the first section, atmosphere matters more than impact. Gradually introduce familiar dark-pop and classic spooky references, then move into House. The final third should increasingly favor percussion, tribal elements and Tech House so the transition into Headliner feels inevitable.

doDont.do: Let early tracks breathe; use recognizable vocals as orientation points; shorten tracks as energy rises.
doDont.dont: Spend Thriller or the strongest peak records here, or push festival-level energy too early.

tracks.artist: Purple Disco Machine & Sophie and the Giants

sections.name: Headliner · Tramo 1
sections.howToUse: The Warm Up has already established the dance pulse. This section tightens the mixes and shortens dead space. Use Latin/tribal percussion to serve the mixed audience, but keep the low end and drum programming coherent. Nightmares is the first major dark marker; it should feel like the door opening into the more explicit Halloween portion.

sections.name: Headliner · Tramo 2 — Halloween / Latin / Tech
sections.howToUse: Halloween becomes obvious here, but thematic records must be separated by groove records. Avoid Halloween-hit stacking. Somebody's Watching Me is the bridge into Peak.

tracks.track: The Addams Family Theme (Tech House / Edit)

sections.name: Headliner · Peak
sections.howToUse: This is the highest-pressure portion. After Somebody's Watching Me, use strong Tech/Electro records to build tension before Thriller. Thriller is the principal Halloween payoff of the show. After it lands, immediately return to groove and crossover House rather than following it with another novelty anthem. The final records remove vocal density and create a clean runway into the Closer.
sections.criticalRule: Thriller gets one principal full-performance slot. Any other Thriller material should be a short tease only, if used at all.

tracks.track: Alternate Latin Tech track — no Frikitona repeat

sections.name: Closer
sections.howToUse: Do not try to outdo the Peak. The job is to convert peak energy into a satisfying ending. Keep people moving, reduce aggression, then reintroduce the Halloween motif. If the crowd still wants celebration, One More Time can stay. If the production needs a darker finish, use the dark/electro alternative instead of stacking multiple euphoric festival records.
sections.finalNarrative: The event begins with Halloween Theme and ultimately returns to Halloween Theme. That callback gives the five-hour program a deliberate beginning, development, climax and ending.

tracks.track: Use instead of a second festival anthem if atmosphere must stay darker
Somebody's Watching Me — 20–30 sec reprise / acapella only

reserve.label: Halloween Reserve / Quick Exit
reserve.note: Keep these tracks in a separate Serato crate. They are not part of the fixed master sequence. Use them when production asks for an immediate energy change, the crowd profile shifts, you need a universally recognizable record, or the event must end earlier than expected.

quickExitProtocol.action: Choose one recognizable Halloween hit → move to This Is Halloween or a short dark bridge → Halloween Theme outro.
Finish the current phrase cleanly → Halloween Theme House/Outro Edit → cinematic original/FX ending.
Heads Will Roll (A-Trak Remix), Firestarter or another compatible high-energy edit; then return to the master at a harmonically and rhythmically sensible point.

seratoExecutionNotes.crates: 01 WARM UP · 02 HEADLINER A · 03 HEADLINER B · 04 PEAK · 05 CLOSER · 06 HALLOWEEN RESERVE · 07 FX / INTROS / OUTROS.
seratoExecutionNotes.tagging: Tag tracks by function: ATMOSPHERE, GROOVE, LATIN/TRIBAL, DARK, HALLOWEEN MARKER, ENERGY UP, CROWD RECOGNITION, EXIT. Add cue points for vocal entry, clean 16/32-bar mix-in, main drop, safe mix-out and any Halloween FX moment.
seratoExecutionNotes.warning: Before showtime, analyze the exact files you will use in Serato. BPM can differ between originals, edits and remixes; the DJ file in your library is the final technical authority for beatgrid and cue placement.
seratoExecutionNotes.timingControl: The five-hour duration is controlled by performance, not track count alone. Use longer blends and full arrangements early; shorten transitions and use more active mixing as the energy rises. Carry approximately 45 minutes of reserve music so production delays or extensions do not force repetition.
seratoExecutionNotes.masterRule: Protect the arc. Warm Up creates expectation. Headliner delivers groove and theme. Peak supplies the major payoff. Closer gives the audience a deliberate ending.
